items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: the years spent with Aretha... I had more problems than a barrel of monkeys on the personal side but that’s what I had to learn to live with. Aretha is one of the best, one of the best performers in the world.

ctx.x: That’s very interesting. So often times you might not hear the final product. You might be in your car driving along and the first time you hear that song that you played on might be on a car radio?

Yeah. And to give you a good example, one of the best examples in the world is Aretha Franklin. “Oh Me Oh My,” “Until You Come Back to Me,” I mean I can — “Rock Steady,” “Daydreaming,” “Think.” I mean all these things happened after the rhythm section was put down. But I got it from her. When she sat down at the piano and played the melody. And where she wanted things to happen and to go. And I was dictating to © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

everybody — by this time I mean I’m hot stuff now man. Oh this Bernard Purdie man. I got all this stuff now. I mean I’m good at what I do, people know I’m good at what I do, so I’m going to get the respect of what I say they’re going to try and don’t let me have no frown or something on my face. “Oh my God Purdie don’t like it. He’s the hit maker. If he don’t like it, it ain’t right.” I mean I had that kind of reputation. So I had to keep my reputation going. And as they say the rest becomes history. Because this…
